source.title: Optimizing Multi-GPU Parallelization Strategies for Deep Learning Training
source.authors: Saptadeep Pal; E. Ebrahimi; Arslan Zulfiqar; Yaosheng Fu; Victor Zhang; Szymon Migacz; D. Nellans; Puneet Gupta

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies global batch size and reports epochs to reach target metrics, a different measure of batch-size effects on training efficiency than held-out performance.
record.gate_note: Results on global batch size and epochs to target metrics bear on V5. The paper does not report fixed-epoch held-out performance; its claims about generalization are not direct test-error measurements. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses large-batch statistical efficiency loss to motivate and project hybrid parallelization speedups. Its own batch-size results measure epochs to a target or convergence failure, rather than held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget. Inception-V3 explicitly uses training loss; the evaluation splits for BLEU and perplexity are unspecified. These results do not establish V5's generalization penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that combining model and data parallelism can improve training time when data-parallel scaling and statistical efficiency deteriorate. They project improvements of at least 26.5%, 8% and 22% for Inception-V3, GNMT and BigLSTM, respectively.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies distributed parallelization and convergence efficiency, measuring epochs to target metrics rather than the claim's fixed-epoch held-out performance. It emulates larger global batches with delayed gradient updates on a four-GPU system and tunes some learning-rate schedules for large batches.
record.method_sensitivity: Global batch size/GPU count changes the reported epochs to target; GNMT's early decrease is attributed to hyperparameters tuned for large global batches.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches increase epochs to the chosen targets for Inception-V3, GNMT and BigLSTM beyond workload-dependent scales. BigLSTM needs 3.2 times as many epochs at 32-way versus 16-way data parallelism and fails to converge within the authors' time limit beyond 32-way.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing global batch size can reduce convergence efficiency, even with learning-rate schedules adapted for larger batches.

fits_no_version.finding: GNMT requires slightly fewer epochs to target BLEU when increasing from two to four workers, using hyperparameters tuned for larger batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size effects on epochs to a target depend on the workload and training recipe.

record.problems: The paper assumes scaling efficiency of 1 for projected comparisons at larger device counts. Larger global batches are emulated on a four-GPU system using delayed gradient updates. The relevant reported outcome is epochs to a target metric, not held-out error at a fixed epoch budget; no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional batch-size outcome rows were omitted; several exact epoch counts are presented only in Figure 4 and are not recoverable from the text.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under different tuning regimes.
Held-out performance at fixed epoch budgets across batch sizes, and whether longer training or recipe adaptations remove a held-out penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains no additional own-result comparison that establishes any claim version. Statements attributing poor generalization to large batches rely on prior work; the study's convergence measurements do not independently verify that attribution.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance.
Fixed-epoch held-out performance, workload-dependent batch thresholds, and comparisons of adapted versus unadapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Inception-V3
rows.stage_stated: trained on ImageNet until a training loss of 6.1 is achieved
rows.operation_detail: Increased global batch size by emulating larger data-parallel GPU counts; measured epochs to target.
rows.measure: Epochs required to hit the target metric
rows.note: The text states the count increases sharply from four to seven beyond global batch size 2048, then grows to 23 at 16384. The reported metric is epochs to target, not held-out performance.
rows.check: Epochs to training loss 6.1 cannot establish held-out performance. The baseline is also misassigned: the text places the increase from four to seven epochs beyond batch size 2048; seven epochs is not the stated value at 2048. The 23-epoch value at 16384 is correct.

rows.subject: GNMT
rows.size_stated: 4 LSTM layers of size 1024 in encoder and decoder
rows.stage_stated: trained on WMT’16 German-English until a BLEU score of 21.8 is achieved
rows.operation_detail: Increased global batch size by emulating larger data-parallel GPU counts; measured epochs to target.
rows.measure: Epochs required to reach target BLEU score
rows.value: Epoch count decreases slightly when going from two to four GPUs
rows.note: The direction at this interval is a slight decrease, not a large-batch penalty.
rows.check: A slight decrease in epochs to target BLEU does not establish absence of a fixed-budget generalization penalty. The evaluation split is unspecified, and GNMT is a translation system rather than the language-model workload named in V5.

rows.subject: GNMT
rows.size_stated: 4 LSTM layers of size 1024 in encoder and decoder
rows.stage_stated: trained on WMT’16 German-English until a BLEU score of 21.8 is achieved
rows.operation_detail: Increased global batch size by emulating larger data-parallel GPU counts; measured epochs to target.
rows.measure: Epochs required to reach target BLEU score
rows.value: The number of epochs required grows rapidly
rows.note: The authors state the hyperparameters were tuned for larger batch sizes; no numeric epoch counts are given for this interval.
rows.check: Increasing epochs to target BLEU measures convergence efficiency. It does not report fixed-budget held-out performance; the evaluation split is unspecified and GNMT is a translation system.

rows.subject: BigLSTM
rows.size_stated: input embedding layer size 1024; 2 LSTM layers with hidden state size 8192; Softmax projection layer size 1024
rows.stage_stated: trained on the 1 billion word language modelling dataset to a perplexity of 67
rows.operation_detail: Increased global batch size by emulating larger data-parallel GPU counts; measured epochs to target.
rows.measure: Epochs required to reach target perplexity
rows.value: 3.2 times the number of epochs is required for 32-way DP compared to 16-way DP
rows.note: Reports convergence efficiency, not fixed-epoch held-out performance.
rows.check: The 3.2-fold increase in epochs to perplexity 67 is correctly reported, but the perplexity evaluation split is unspecified. Epochs to this target cannot establish V5's held-out penalty.

rows.subject: BigLSTM
rows.size_stated: input embedding layer size 1024; 2 LSTM layers with hidden state size 8192; Softmax projection layer size 1024
rows.stage_stated: trained on the 1 billion word language modelling dataset to a perplexity of 67
rows.operation_detail: Increased global batch size by emulating larger data-parallel GPU counts; measured convergence.
rows.measure: Whether training converged within a meaningful time limit
rows.value: Training did not converge within a meaningful time limit
rows.note: This is an explicit convergence failure at larger scale; no fixed-epoch test metric is reported.
rows.check: Failure to converge within an unspecified time limit does not measure held-out performance under a fixed epoch budget. The stopping budget and attained perplexity are unreported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Inception-V3 at global batch sizes beyond 2048, GNMT beyond 64 GPUs, and BigLSTM at 32-way or greater DP
reader_labels.reason: Reported epochs to target rise sharply for Inception-V3 and BigLSTM and rapidly for GNMT, but the paper does not directly measure fixed-epoch held-out performance (R1, R3, R4, R5). The batch-size effect is also not uniform: GNMT's epoch count decreases slightly from two to four GPUs (R2).
